title: These US Cities Spend the Most on Groceries
paragraphs: Grocery prices are rising around the world. There are many reasons for this, including rising fuel costs, climate change and global instability, and the exact rise in prices can be very different depending on where you live.
Finance app WalletHub has put together a list of cities where Americans are spending the most and least amount of their money on groceries.

It looked at the prices of 26 common grocery items across 100 of the largest US cities. It added up the cost of those items and compared that with the average household income in each city, to see where people are spending the largest share of their money at the grocery store.
Detroit, Michigan, is at the top of the list, with residents needing to spend more than 4% of the city's average household income to buy the 26 common grocery items.
Fremont, California, has the lowest spending as a percentage of income, at less than 1%.
That doesn't mean Detroit has the highest overall prices, though. Looking at the specific prices of those 26 grocery items, Detroit is actually just the 39th most expensive city.

However, the city has the lowest average annual household income in America, at just under $40,000 — while Fremont's is over $160,000. This means people in Detroit have to spend a higher percentage of their income on groceries compared to people in higher-earning cities.

The situation is similar in Cleveland, Ohio, where residents spend the second-largest percentage of their income on groceries — just under 4%. Cleveland actually has relatively low prices for a number of items on the grocery list, but it also has the second-lowest average household income, at just under $41,000 per year.
Birmingham, Alabama, is in third place, with residents needing to spend 3.5% of their average $46,000 income on groceries.
